description: `total` is how many rows matched, not how many the page holds. LIMIT bounds delivery; it is the only thing an agent has to tell a first page from a whole answer, and a total clipped to the page size says: this is all of it, about every first page. These cases pin the count against a ground truth taken at a limit high enough that nothing pages at all. Two mechanisms had to change for that and each has its own case: the clause pipeline now reports its size before OFFSET and LIMIT cut it, and the running top-K trim counts the rows it discards on rank. The name-index streams are the third mechanism: they answer from the per-segment deduplicated row counts stored at overlay build time, and their cases ask a five-row page to carry the size of the whole corpus. The segment fetch cap that used to be the other such place is gone: a bare LIMIT is now trimmed by the same running top-K as an ordered one, because the pipeline sorts by (name, line, path, fql_kind) even with no ORDER BY, and the four cases in clause_pipeline.json that pinned the cap are enforced rather than expected to fail. Both mechanisms were checked by mutation rather than assumed: with the trim's count disabled the same query reads '1 of 2 shown' through the built binary on the sibling workspace and '1 of 8 shown' with it on, against an unlimited answer of 8. What no case here can see is whether the collapse that now runs before the trim is reached at all, because it is defined not to move answers; that was measured separately with a panic in place -- one ordinary query collapsed 8 of 108 row ids inside a single segment, before any of them was built -- and it is pinned by the unit tests in fast_paths/tests.rs, which do go red. The FIND usages cases are the same contract in a different unit: there LIMIT counts files, so a page and its total answer different questions by construction. Where the cut is made is not something they can see — the caller-side selection they replaced produced the same numbers — and the unit suite is what pins that. One verb this suite cannot reach at all is SHOW COMMITS, which counts the commits the session itself made: a golden session makes none, and one that committed would meet the commit gate. Its total is pinned by show_commits_reports_every_commit_not_the_page_size in crates/forgeql-core/tests/checkpoint_persist.rs, where a session can commit.

cases.name: the_answer_this_suite_measures_against
cases.description: Ground truth. Seven functions in this corpus exceed 150 lines, and every total below is this seven. It reaches that answer over row views, like almost every case here: a page is now cut from views whatever its limit, so a limit above TOPK_THRESHOLD no longer means every matching row is built -- it means the built-row trim is not what bounds it. What the limit still buys is that nothing is shed or truncated, since 1001 is past the answer's own size.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: a_page_reports_the_size_of_the_answer_it_came_from
cases.description: LIMIT 2 over the same seven rows. Two rows come back and the count says seven. K * TOPK_OVER_FETCH is eight here, so the working set never reaches the trim's threshold and nothing is shed — this case isolates the pipeline's own count, taken before OFFSET and LIMIT rather than after them.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 2

cases.name: the_running_trim_counts_what_it_sheds
cases.description: The same seven rows at LIMIT 1, which puts K * TOPK_OVER_FETCH at four and so does arm the shedding: the working set passes four while the segments are still being read and is cut back, and then cut once more to the one row the page holds. Those discarded rows never reach the clause pipeline, so the pipeline's own count cannot see them and the scan has to hand back how many it dropped. Without that the answer here reads as four rows, or two, or one — the size of a window nobody asked for. The shedding runs over row views on this query and over built rows where a predicate keeps it off them, with one comparator and one count between the two, which the case below holds it to. The rows are distinct because duplicates are collapsed before anything sheds; that is what makes them countable at all.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 1

cases.name: a_name_ordered_stream_counts_the_answer_it_streams_from
cases.description: The streams answer the count without the walk. `ORDER BY name [DESC]`, with at most an `fql_kind` equality beside it, streams the name FST in order and stops after LIMIT + OFFSET rows -- but every segment's deduplicated row count was stored when the overlay was built, and a kind-filtered stream's bitmap knows its own cardinality, so the total beside the streamed page is the corpus's answer, not the page. This shape used to be the last surviving member of the family this suite exists to kill -- an early exit that assumes LIMIT bounds the answer, reporting total: 5 on this corpus of 59636 rows -- and was pinned here as an expected failure until the stored counts closed it. Where those counts cannot speak for the answer, two segments built from one source path, the streams decline and the pipeline answers; the unit suites pin that decline.
cases.fql: FIND symbols ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 5

cases.name: a_bare_limit_answers_from_the_stream_with_the_same_total
cases.description: The shortest query an agent can type, served by the same ascending stream: with no ORDER BY written the pipeline's default ordering starts with name, so the page is the ORDER BY name page and the total is the same stored corpus count. Before the stream claimed this shape it materialised every row in the corpus to deliver five of them.

cases.name: the_pipeline_counts_the_same_corpus
cases.description: Ground truth for the two stream cases above, through a route no stream serves: a WHERE clause declines the name streams, and line >= 1 matches every row -- lines are 1-based -- so this is the full scan's collapsed count of the same corpus. If the stored per-segment counts and the pipeline's collapse ever disagree, the three cases split here.

cases.name: the_usages_default_page_is_twenty_files_not_twenty_rows
cases.description: FIND usages pages by FILE. Thirty files of this corpus hold the name and the default page renders the first twenty of them whole -- ninety-eight sites -- while total stays the true site count across all thirty. The four cases here pin the answer, and only the answer. They cannot see WHERE the cut is made: the caller-side selection this replaced produced these same numbers, so a page cut in the engine layer would satisfy every one of them. What the bound reaching the backend buys — a result row built only for the sites inside the page — is not pinned exactly anywhere: the nearest is a_bounded_page_renders_whole_files_and_still_counts_the_rest in crates/forgeql-core/src/storage/mod.rs, which asks for zero files and gets zero rows DELIVERED with the count intact, and a regression that built all five and discarded them would satisfy that too. The count of rows built is held by construction — one call site, mapping over the selection.

cases.name: an_explicit_usages_limit_counts_files_too
cases.description: Three files, every site of each, and the count unchanged. A row LIMIT would have returned three rows and reported a file as partly used with nothing to say it did; this is the unit that replaced it, and it is the reason FIND usages cannot take the row bound FIND symbols hands its engine.

cases.name: a_usages_predicate_is_answered_before_the_page_is_cut
cases.description: WHERE role = 'code' drops forty-nine of the hundred and seventy-two sites, and the total reports the hundred and twenty-three that survive rather than everything the name matched. The same three files come back whole and the row count is unchanged, because every site in those three is already role code — so this case separates the count from the page and nothing more. That the predicate runs over the sites ahead of the file selection is not visible here and is not claimed here.
cases.fql: FIND usages OF 'SymbolMatch' WHERE role = 'code' LIMIT 3

cases.name: an_offset_on_usages_skips_whole_files
cases.description: OFFSET is in files as well: skipping one and taking two lands on the second and third files, twelve sites between them, with the count still the whole answer. File order never changes, so a page and its successor partition the files rather than overlapping.

cases.name: the_default_page_is_a_bound_the_engine_is_told_about
cases.description: No LIMIT written. The engine used to build every matching row and the twenty-row default was cut afterwards, so this query materialised rows up to the row budget to show twenty; the default page is now handed to the engine as the LIMIT an explicit `LIMIT 20` would carry, and it takes the same name stream. Twenty rows, and the total is the whole corpus -- the same 59636 the explicit-LIMIT stream and the pipeline report above -- because the bound changes what is held, never what is counted.

cases.name: the_default_page_under_a_predicate_rides_the_running_trim
cases.description: The same default page through the pipeline: a WHERE declines the name streams, so the bound cuts the page from row views instead. Every row is still read and counted; twenty are built. Same total as every other case on this corpus.

cases.name: the_same_total_when_a_regex_keeps_the_query_off_the_view_route
cases.description: The same seven-row answer counted by the route that builds as it goes. `name MATCHES '^'` matches every name -- the empty pattern anchors at position 0 of any string -- so the rows are exactly the ground truth's, and the operator is what changes the route: a regular expression is compiled once for a batch of built rows rather than once per row, so it is deferred past materialisation on every segment and no page can be cut from views ahead of it. The pair is the only cross-route claim this suite can make from the agent side. A golden case cannot list a frozen corpus's page, so 'the two routes return the same rows' is pinned by construction -- the same clauses reach the engine -- plus these counts; what does go red when the routes disagree is the unit suite in fast_paths/tests.rs.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 WHERE name MATCHES '^' ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 1

cases.name: an_offset_page_counts_the_answer_it_came_from
cases.description: An OFFSET never armed the running trim over built rows -- shedding on rank is unsound while a skip is still to come -- so this shape used to build every matching row. It rides views now, which carry LIMIT + OFFSET of them because the skip runs downstream, after a session's uncommitted rows have been merged in. Two rows delivered, and the count is still the whole answer.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 2 OFFSET 2
